title: The Limits Of Economic Fury
gist: A Gavekal teaser argues the US, after a five-week 'kinetic' bombing campaign against Iran (Operation Epic Fury) ended April 7, is pivoting to a campaign of 'economic fury' to force Tehran to concede. It contends this economic phase is no more likely to yield a quick US win, but that the market impact is overstated: Iran is not near collapse and regional energy-trade disruption is smaller than feared. (Byline in text: Tom Holland; the raw author field is empty.)

insights.claim: Trump said in early March that Operation Epic Fury, the US military campaign against Iran, could last four to five weeks, and the 'kinetic' bombing phase did last five weeks before the US suspended its nightly raids on April 7.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Establishes the timeline and confirms the shooting war ended in early April without a decisive outcome, framing the shift to non-military tools that markets now must price.

insights.so_what: Signals the conflict is moving from bombs to sanctions/economic pressure, a regime that plays out over quarters and shapes oil and EM risk premia rather than causing acute supply shocks.
